To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dry powder inhalation device (Turbohaler) for inhalation of budesonide and terbutaline, when used in the recommended manner, is an efficient and safe method of drug delivery to the airways.

the inhalation technique of a metered-dose inhaler is crucial for the efficacy and side effects, that a low flow rate is not necessary for the inhalation of a powder inhaler device, that an exhalation to the residual volume prior to inhalation is not necessary, and that an exhalational breath through the device is not recommended.

the efficacy of a dry powder inhalation device for terbutaline is not dependent on inhalation flow, but that the inhalation volume should be as high as possible and the exhalation volume as low as possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhalation technique and the mode of inhalatory administration of a dry powder inhalation device for inhalation therapy in asthma.
the effects of different modes of inhalations on bronchodilation and the side-effects of terbutalinesulphate inhaled by means of the TBH, a new dry powder device.
the inhalation technique of the TBH and the effect on pulmonary function and side effects of terbutalinesulphate inhaled from the TBH in adult asthmatic subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhalation of terbulatine from a TBH is highly effective and safe, irrespective of the mode of inhalatory manoeuvre.

the mode of inhalations with the terbutalines Turbohaler should be standardized to an inspiratory flow of approximately 34 l/min, a volume of approximately 0.5 l and a preceding exhalation to total lung capacity.
inhalation through a TBH at a low inspiratory flow is as efficient as at a high flow, but with a slightly reduced side effect profile and lower plasma concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TBH is very easy to use and the efficacy is not dependent on the mode and volume of inhalation, but the inhalation flow must be at least 34 l min.
the TBH, as well as most dry powder inhaler devices, can be used at a variety of inhalation flows and inspiratory volumes, and that a previous exhalatory manoeuvre is not necessary.
, when the TBH is used, a flow of at least 50 l min-1 is required to achieve the full bronchodilation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TBH can be inhaled with the same effect at flows varying between 34-88 l min- 1.
the TBH is an efficient device for inhalation therapy of asthma, and that the inhalation technique is not critical.
the use of a dry powder inhalation device is not a panacea for the management of asthma.
